title: A new AI listens to every prison call and decides who is speaking

content_html:
A Texas company has begun selling corrections agencies an artificial intelligence system that listens to prison phone calls. It works out who is speaking, whether or not the speaker wants that.

LEO Technologies, based in Austin, announced Verus Voice AI on Monday. The product uses voice biometrics to catch prisoners who call on someone else’s personal identification number. It builds and tracks voice identities continuously, the company says, rather than waiting for staff to spot anomalies.

“Personal identification codes and phones can be shared, coerced, or swapped amongst inmates,” said Tim Anderson. “But a voice can’t be.” Anderson is a senior vice president at the firm.

Two descriptions of the same product

The press release stresses restraint. It says the system carries “built-in safeguards”, and that qualified personnel review every finding before anyone acts. The company promises “human oversight and accountability” throughout.

Its own product page makes a wider promise. The page invites agencies to “upload any voice sample and instantly search for matches across all conversations”. That, it says, eliminates manual verification.

The 💜 of EU tech

The latest rumblings from the EU tech scene, a story from our wise ol' founder Boris, and some questionable AI art. It's free, every week, in your inbox. Sign up now!

A companion page for the firm’s voice biometrics line is blunter. It reads: “Identify who’s speaking, even when they don’t want to be identified.”

Those are not descriptions of a PIN checker. They describe a searchable archive of voices, queryable against any sample an investigator supplies.

Fifteen years of voiceprints

Voice biometrics in American jails are not new. Securus Technologies has sold a product called Investigator Pro for over a decade. It markets the tool on nearly identical terms: detecting PIN abuse and recognising callers.

In 2019, The Appeal and The Intercept reported that institutions had built databases of hundreds of thousands of voiceprints. They found jails in Arizona, Texas, New Mexico, Michigan, Florida, Massachusetts, Colorado and Wisconsin buying the technology.

Much of that collection covered people awaiting trial. Officials at the Fort Bend County jail in Texas said the facility printed everyone who came through the door. A print then stayed in the system after release, unless an expunction order arrived. The vendor held the data on its own network, not the county’s.

Consent, in a place with very little of it

Civil liberties lawyers have long argued that such agreement means little. Aaron Mackey of the Electronic Frontier Foundation told The Appeal that jail voiceprinting could amount to illegal search and seizure. People submit, he said, because refusing costs them contact with their families.

Senator Ron Wyden, an Oregon Democrat, raised the commercial question. If Securus profits from biometric data the government seizes, he said, “Americans have a right to know”.

Clare Garvie, then at Georgetown Law’s Center on Privacy and Technology, went further. Agencies should destroy biometric templates, she argued, when prosecutors drop charges or a jury acquits. Several defence lawyers said nobody had told them the prints existed.

The other voice on the line

Every monitored call has at least two people on it. Only one is a prisoner. The EFF has noted that this class of technology could profile anyone whose voice crosses into a prison. That includes the parents, children and friends of the people inside.

LEO Technologies has not said whether Verus Voice AI enrols or keeps the voices of people outside the facility. Its announcement gives no retention period, no deletion process, and no storage location. Neither does the product page.

The gap matters because voice analysis rarely stops at identity. Meta has patented mood tracking from voice, and consumer tools now record conversations by default. Anthropic began collecting biometric data from flagged users this year.

The case for it

The problem the product targets is real. Phone minutes work as currency inside facilities, and prisoners trade, borrow and seize each other’s PINs. Investigators also use call monitoring to detect witness intimidation and the harassment of domestic violence victims. Securus cited exactly that in 2019 when it defended its own system.

LEO Technologies frames its platform around safety rather than punishment. The line includes video analysis, an operations dashboard, and a wellness tool for suicide prevention. Steven Harpe, its chief product officer, said earlier tools had been “too expensive and too unreliable”.

Accuracy remains the awkward part. The Appeal watched a Fort Bend sergeant review calls that Investigator Pro had flagged. The system rated its own matches at 83, 79, 55 and 45 percent. The sergeant accepted that defence lawyers could challenge such evidence, then sent the recordings to prosecutors anyway.

Already on the shelf

Verus Voice AI is on sale now. LEO Technologies holds a General Services Administration schedule contract and three Texas state purchasing contracts. Agencies can therefore buy it through existing routes, without a fresh procurement or a public debate.

That mechanism matters more than any single launch. It is how Flock’s camera network spread across American towns, and how facial recognition reached British high streets.

Bianca Tylek of the Corrections Accountability Project made the point in 2019, and it has aged well. Firms test this kind of system on people the public tends to treat as having forfeited their rights. “Today it’s this population,” she said, “but tomorrow it’s another.”

content_html_zh:
德克萨斯州的一家公司已开始向惩教机构出售一种可以监听监狱电话的人工智能系统。 它可以确定谁在讲话，无论讲话者是否愿意。

总部位于奥斯汀的 LEO Technologies 于周一宣布推出 Verus Voice AI。 该产品使用语音生物识别技术来捕捉拨打他人个人身份证号码的囚犯。 该公司表示，它会持续构建和跟踪语音身份，而不是等待员工发现异常情况。

“囚犯之间可以共享、胁迫或交换个人识别码和电话，”蒂姆·安德森说。 “但声音不可能。” 安德森是该公司的高级副总裁。

同一产品的两种描述

新闻稿强调克制。 据称，该系统具有“内置保障措施”，合格人员会在任何人采取行动之前审查每项发现。 该公司自始至终承诺“人为监督和问责”。

它自己的产品页面做出了更广泛的承诺。 该页面邀请代理机构“上传任何语音样本并立即在所有对话中搜索匹配项”。 它说，这消除了手动验证。

欧盟科技的💜

来自欧盟科技界的最新传言、我们明智的创始人鲍里斯的故事，以及一些值得怀疑的人工智能艺术。 每周都会免费发送到您的收件箱中。 立即注册！

该公司语音生物识别产品线的配套页面较为直白。 上面写着：“识别谁在说话，即使他们不想被识别。”

这些不是 PIN 检查器的描述。 他们描述了一个可搜索的声音档案，可以根据调查人员提供的任何样本进行查询。

十五年的声纹

美国监狱中的语音生物识别技术并不新鲜。 Securus Technologies 销售一款名为 Investigator Pro 的产品已有十多年了。 它以几乎相同的术语推销该工具：检测 PIN 滥用和识别呼叫者。

2019 年，The Appeal 和 The Intercept 报道称，各机构已经建立了包含数十万个声纹的数据库。 他们发现亚利桑那州、德克萨斯州、新墨西哥州、密歇根州、佛罗里达州、马萨诸塞州、科罗拉多州和威斯康星州的监狱购买了这项技术。

其中大部分藏品涵盖了等待审判的人。 德克萨斯州本德堡县监狱的官员表示，该设施打印了所有进门的人。 除非收到删除命令，否则打印件发布后会保留在系统中。 供应商将数据保存在自己的网络上，而不是县的网络上。

同意，在一个很少有同意的地方

公民自由律师长期以来一直认为，这种协议意义不大。 电子前沿基金会的亚伦·麦基 (Aaron Mackey) 告诉《上诉报》，监狱声纹识别可能构成非法搜查和扣押。 他说，人们会屈服，因为拒绝会让他们失去与家人的联系。

俄勒冈州民主党参议员罗恩·怀登提出了商业问题。 他说，如果 Securus 从政府夺取的生物识别数据中获利，“美国人就有知情权”。

当时在乔治城法律隐私与技术中心工作的克莱尔·加维 (Clare Garvie) 走得更远。 她认为，当检察官撤销指控或陪审团无罪释放时，各机构应该销毁生物识别模板。 几名辩护律师表示，没有人告诉他们这些指纹的存在。

线路上的另一个声音

每个受监控的通话至少有两个人在通话。 只有一个人是囚犯。 EFF 指出，此类技术可以对任何进入监狱的声音进行分析。 其中包括里面人的父母、孩子和朋友。

LEO Technologies 尚未透露 Verus Voice AI 是否会注册或保留设施外人员的声音。 它的公告没有给出保留期限、没有删除过程、也没有给出存储位置。 产品页面也没有。

这种差距很重要，因为语音分析很少停留在身份识别上。 Meta 已获得语音情绪跟踪专利，消费者工具现在默认记录对话。 Anthropic 今年开始收集被标记用户的生物识别数据。

案例

产品所针对的问题是真实存在的。 电话时间在监狱内充当货币，囚犯之间可以交易、借用和扣押彼此的密码。 调查人员还利用通话监控来侦查证人恐吓和家庭暴力受害者的骚扰情况。 Securus 在 2019 年为自己的系统辩护时就引用了这一点。

LEO Technologies 围绕安全而非惩罚构建其平台。 该产品线包括视频分析、操作仪表板和预防自杀的健康工具。 其首席产品官史蒂文·哈普 (Steven Harpe) 表示，早期的工具“太昂贵且太不可靠”。

准确性仍然是尴尬的部分。 上诉观察到本德堡的一名警官审查了调查员 Pro 标记的电话。 该系统对自己的比赛评分分别为 83%、79%、55% 和 45%。 警官承认辩护律师可以对这些证据提出质疑，但无论如何还是将录音发送给了检察官。

已经上架了

Verus Voice AI 现已发售。 LEO Technologies 持有一份总务管理局计划合同和三份德克萨斯州采购合同。 因此，各机构可以通过现有途径购买，无需重新采购或公开辩论。

该机制比任何一次发布都更重要。 这就是弗洛克的摄像头网络如何遍布美国城镇，以及面部识别如何进入英国大街的方式。

惩教问责项目的比安卡·泰莱克 (Bianca Tylek) 在 2019 年提出了这一观点，而且这一观点已经过时了。 公司在公众倾向于视为丧失权利的人身上测试这种系统。 “今天是这个人口，”她说，“但明天又是另一个人口。”
